claims.text: In Pulumi, calling `toString` on an `Output<T>` produces the placeholder text "Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported" instead of the underlying value.

The placeholder text "Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported" can show up in a log line, a generated file, or a resource property when an Output is treated as if it were already a plain value.

The page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ ("Output value errors") exists and describes the `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` symptom and other symptoms of treating an output as if it were already a plain value.

A Pulumi docs troubleshooting page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ covering errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value as if it were a plain value.
In Pulumi programs, stringifying an output value, branching on it (e.g., using it in a conditional), or reading it like a plain value produces errors.

Pulumi (Pulumi Cloud) returns a "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" error when an update is already in progress on a stack; the page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ addresses it.
Pulumi Cloud can return 500 internal server errors, and the page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/server-errors/ covers handling them.
Pulumi can fail with post-step event failures caused by engine bugs; the page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/post-step-errors/ covers troubleshooting them.
A Pulumi docs page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/connection-issues/ covering network connectivity and proxy problems.

The Pulumi CLI emits a `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` error when it cannot access a self-managed (DIY) state backend, and the section 'error-reading-pulumimetayaml' exists on /docs/iac/operations/stack-management/using-a-diy-backend/.
A Pulumi docs page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ covering scenarios in which `pulumi destroy` fails.
A Pulumi docs page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/interrupted-updates/ covering recovery from interrupted deployments.
On Apple Silicon Macs, running x86_64 binaries under Rosetta 2 can cause Pulumi crashes or hangs; the page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/architecture-mismatch/ covers fixing this.
A Pulumi docs page exists at /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/troubleshooting/ covering continuous integration and deployment pipeline issues.
A Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/stack-management/editing-state-files/ describes safe techniques for modifying Pulumi state files.
A recently deleted Pulumi stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
The Pulumi CLI supports `--target` and `--exclude` flags to limit operations to specific resources, and these can be used when a stuck or misbehaving resource is blocking a wider update.
The Pulumi logging docs page covers automatic logging, CLI verbose logging, and program logging for debugging and diagnostics.
Pulumi dev builds are pre-release builds that let users access bug fixes that have not yet shipped in a stable release.
Pulumi has a Community Slack at https://slack.pulumi.com offering community support.
A Pulumi guide for filing GitHub issues exists at /docs/support/filing-issues/ explaining how to report bugs in the right repository.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
The logging guide at /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/ has an 'automatic-logging' section that covers `pulumi logs share`.
Pulumi offers paid support options, reachable via the /contact/ page.
The URL hash '#conflict' on the troubleshooting index page is redirected to /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/, per pulumi/pulumi issue 20846.

The URL hash '#verbose-logging' on the troubleshooting index page is redirected to /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/#cli-verbose-logging, per pulumi/docs issue 16985; the 'cli-verbose-logging' anchor exists on that page.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values, because their real values are not known until the resource providing them has been created or updated.
Representing resource properties as Outputs is central to how Pulumi builds a dependency graph and runs `pulumi preview`.
The Pulumi docs page on inputs and outputs has an '#outputs' section at /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/ that explains Outputs.
The Pulumi docs have pages titled 'Accessing single outputs with Apply' at /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply/ and 'Working with multiple outputs' at /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/all/.

If an output value is concatenated, logged, or otherwise converted to a string directly instead of via `apply` or an equivalent helper, Pulumi does not raise an error by default and instead silently substitutes a placeholder message in place of the value.

In Pulumi TypeScript, interpolating an Output (e.g. `${bucket.bucketName}`) into a template string produces a string containing the literal text `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`, and no exception is thrown.
In Pulumi TypeScript, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an Output, or letting one flow into a JSON body, produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.

In Pulumi Python, using an Output in an f-string produces a string containing the literal text `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported`, Pulumi also logs a warning, and no exception is raised.
In Pulumi Python, passing an Output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`.
In Pulumi Python, `Output.json_dumps()` is the way to serialize an Output to JSON.
In Pulumi Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error, not a runtime surprise.
In Pulumi Go, the value of an output is resolved via `ApplyT`.

In Pulumi C#, interpolating an Output (e.g. `{bucket.BucketName}`) into an interpolated string produces a string containing the literal text `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`, and no exception is thrown.

Because converting an Output to string produces a placeholder rather than throwing, the program runs and `pulumi up` succeeds, with the placeholder text surfacing later in a log line, generated config file, or downstream resource property.

Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` is supported in TypeScript, Python, and C# Pulumi SDKs, and causes the string-conversion code to throw an exception at the point of the mistake instead of returning placeholder text.
`pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` are the string-composition helpers for Outputs in Pulumi TypeScript.
`Output.concat`, `Output.format`, and `Output.json_dumps` are the string-composition helpers for Outputs in Pulumi Python.
`pulumi.Sprintf` and `pulumi.JSONMarshal` are the string-composition helpers for Outputs in Pulumi Go.
`Output.Format` is the string-composition helper for Outputs in Pulumi C#.

The value read from an Output inside an `apply`/`Apply` callback is only available inside that callback (or in another Output derived from it); assigning it to an outer variable and using it outside the callback yields `undefined` in TypeScript because the callback has not yet run.
The `apply` callback runs asynchronously once the Output resolves, which in general is after the program's top-level code has finished running.
The `apply` callback's timing is determined by the Pulumi engine resolving the dependency graph, so adding a delay in the program cannot fix reading the value early.
In Pulumi TypeScript, passing an Output directly (e.g. `bucket.bucketName`) as the `bucket` input of `aws.s3.BucketObject` works without `apply`.
Most Pulumi resource inputs accept Outputs as well as plain values, while a handful of positions such as a resource's logical name cannot accept Outputs.
The page contains a section anchored at '#using-an-output-as-a-resource-name-a-map-key-or-a-loop-bound'.

In a dynamically typed Pulumi language, an `if` on an Output evaluates the Output object itself rather than its eventual value, so the condition is generally always true regardless of what the Output resolves to.
In a statically typed Pulumi language, branching on an `Output<bool>` is usually a compile error because an `Output<bool>` is not a `bool`.
A value known when the program starts, such as a stack configuration setting read with `pulumi.Config`, an environment variable, or a hardcoded flag, is a plain value and can be branched on normally.
When a branch depends on a resource's Output, the branch must move inside `apply`, expressing both outcomes as values rather than program structure.

Because branches on an Output cannot be expressed as separate blocks of resource-creation code, a runtime branch on an Output usually requires restructuring the program so both sets of resources are described unconditionally, or branching on a plain config value instead.

A resource's logical name (the first constructor argument), loop bounds, and map keys used while authoring a program must be known plain values while the program is being evaluated, before any resource exists.
Passing an Output as a resource's logical name, loop bound, or map key fails to compile in Pulumi TypeScript, Go, and C#, where these positions are typed as plain strings or numbers.
In Pulumi Python, passing an Output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, using a Pulumi Output as a loop bound (`range(some_output)`) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Pulumi Python, using an Output as a dictionary key does not raise; Python falls back to comparing and hashing the Output object itself, so the lookup silently keys on the wrong thing.

When resource names or counts need data only known after a resource is created, one fix is to provision the dependent resources in a later, separate stack that consumes the first stack's outputs through a `StackReference`.
The Pulumi docs describe `StackReference` at /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/#stackreferences.
Trying to `await` a Pulumi Output or read its value synchronously either doesn't compile, fails at runtime, or quietly returns placeholder text instead of the value.

Pulumi has no supported way to block the program and synchronously pull a resolved value out of an Output, deliberately, because the engine would need the value before it has finished determining the order to create resources.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output from the CLI after a deployment.
A `StackReference` from another Pulumi program consumes one stack's outputs as another stack's inputs.
The Pulumi Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (e.g. `res.Outputs` in Go), usable when driving deployments programmatically.
The Pulumi docs have an Automation API page at /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.
`pulumi stack output`, `StackReference`, and the Automation API outputs all read a value that has already resolved, rather than unwrapping an in-flight Output from inside the same program.
